sisyphus.prompt_append: Follow the "OmO and focused-spec Executable Specifications" section of the root AGENTS.md. For explicitly requested specification work, load the focused-spec skill: when authoring requirements, write scenarios and run non-strict validation; when implementing, run acceptance for the corresponding scope. Handle simple tasks without a specification in the normal way. Do not start planning or implementation without a matching user request.

prometheus.prompt_append: Follow the "OmO and focused-spec Executable Specifications" section of the root AGENTS.md. When the plan is built from an approved specification, load the focused-spec skill, read the specification and map every scenario ID to plan tasks. Make replacing planned: evidence with real tests and running focused-spec run --scope <scope> mandatory acceptance steps alongside the normal OmO checks. For a change specification under specs/changes/, also make closing the change mandatory: merge its scenarios into the capability owners, archive it under specs/archive/ and run focused-spec run --scope <capability> for every affected owner. Do not edit the specification outside the planner's permitted paths and do not delegate such edits: report required amendments to the user. Do not start implementation. The mere presence of focused-spec configuration does not enable SDD.

atlas.prompt_append: Follow the "OmO and focused-spec Executable Specifications" section of the root AGENTS.md. When the plan references a specification, load the focused-spec skill and pass executors the specification path, scope, scenario IDs and acceptance criteria. Do not mark implementation complete until planned: evidence is replaced and focused-spec run --scope <scope> succeeds on the accepted code revision and, for a change specification, the change is closed into its capability owners per AGENTS.md and their focused-spec run passes. SKIP, a missing test or a check that was not run is not a pass. Keep the normal OmO builds, regression checks and QA; do not apply SDD to unrelated tasks.
